answer.rationale: Memory 57 is strongest because it explicitly reports qualified-revenue gains and no measurable retention harm, directly addressing both revenue quality and sustainability. Memory 44 supports qualified pipeline quality but omits closed-won revenue, retention, and economics. Memory 73 shows acquisition and revenue lift in the relevant price-sensitive SMB segment, but targeted discounting lacks evidence on margin, retention, or long-run durability. Memories 86 and 91 show adoption and engagement improvements that are plausible leading indicators, but do not establish qualified-revenue or retention impact. Memory 31 is least supported because it establishes only first-week activation from simplified signup, with no evidence on downstream monetization, customer quality, retention, or durable revenue.
